facts.statement: Scolosaurus was first described by Franz Nopcsa in 1928.
facts.quote: authority: Nopcsa, 1928

facts.statement: Scolosaurus fossils are found in the Late Cretaceous (about 76.5 million years ago) of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: It is known from the lower levels of the Dinosaur Park Formation and upper levels of the Oldman Formation in the Late Cretaceous (latest middle Campanian stage, about 76.5 Ma ago) of Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: The type species Scolosaurus cutleri grew up to 5.6 meters long and weighed 2.2 metric tons.
facts.quote: The type species, S. cutleri, measured up to 5.6 m in length and 2.2 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Scolosaurus is NHMUK PV R.5161, housed in the Natural History Museum in London.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus was named by Franz Nopcsa von Felső-Szilvás in 1928, based on holotype NHMUK PV R.5161

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was discovered by collector William Edmund Cutler in 1914 at Deadlodge Canyon.
facts.quote: The fossil skeleton was discovered by William Edmund Cutler, an independent fossil collector in 1914 at Quarry 80 of the Deadlodge Canyon locality.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen preserves rare osteoderms and skin impressions.
facts.quote: The rare preservation of osteoderms and skin impression are also present.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus is classified as an ankylosaurid dinosaur in the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the genus Oohkotokia is synonymous with Scolosaurus.
facts.quote: Some researchers have considered the genus Oohkotokia, known from the also Campanian-aged Two Medicine Formation of Montana, United States, to be synonymous with Scolosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers distinguish Scolosaurus from Euoplocephalus based on cervical armor, general armor details, and forelimb structure.
facts.quote: They concluded that Scolosaurus can be distinguished from Euoplocephalus by the form of their cervical armour, the details of other armour and the structure of the forelimb.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus is considered distinct from Dyoplosaurus due to differences in the pelvis and armor.
facts.quote: They also concluded that Scolosaurus and Dyoplosaurus are distinct, due to differences noted in the pelvis and armour.

facts.statement: The name Scolosaurus means "pointed stake lizard", derived from Greek words for stake and lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name Scolosaurus means "pointed stake lizard" and is derived from the Greek words skolos (σκῶλος) meaning "pointed stake", and saûros (σαύρα) meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: Scolosaurus possesses backswept squamosal horns with distinct tips that are proportionately longer than in related species.
facts.quote: the squamosal horns are proportionately longer, are backswept, and have distinct apices

facts.statement: The tail club knob of Scolosaurus appears circular when viewed from above.
facts.quote: the tail club knob appears circular in dorsal view

facts.statement: Scolosaurus has nostrils (nares) that face forward.
facts.quote: the presence of anteriorly-directed nares

facts.statement: Specimen USNM 7943 was excavated by G. M. Dawson in 1874 from the Frenchman Formation in Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1874, G. M. Dawson excavated specimen USNM 7943 at the Milk River locality of the Frenchman Formation in Alberta.

facts.statement: The habitat of Scolosaurus featured a seasonal, semi-arid climate with warm temperatures and long dry seasons.
facts.quote: Lithologies, invertebrate faunas, and plant and pollen data support that the Two Medicine Formation was deposited in a seasonal, semi-arid climate with possible rainshadows from the Cordilleran highlands.

facts.statement: Volcanic eruptions periodically blanketed the Scolosaurus habitat with ash, causing mass mortality but also enriching the soil for plant growth.
facts.quote: Volcanic eruptions from the west periodically blanketed the region with ash, resulting in large-scale mortality, while simultaneously enriching the soil for future plant growth.

facts.statement: Fluctuating sea levels created diverse environments for Scolosaurus, including marine habitats, coastal wetlands, deltas, lagoons, and inland floodplains.
facts.quote: Fluctuating sea levels also resulted in a variety of other environments at different times and places within the Judith River Group, including offshore and nearshore marine habitats, coastal wetlands, deltas and lagoons, in addition to the inland floodplains.

facts.statement: Fossilized eggs of a dromaeosaur have been recovered from the same region where Scolosaurus fossils are found.
facts.quote: Fossilized eggs belonging to a dromaeosaur have been recovered here.

facts.statement: The genus Scolosaurus was named by Nopcsa in 1928.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Nopcsa, 1928

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Scolosaurus is Scolosaurus cutleri.
facts.quote: type_species: Scolosaurus cutleri

facts.statement: A second species, Scolosaurus thronus, was described by Penkalski in 2013.
facts.quote: subdivision: Scolosaurus thronus Penkalski, 2013

facts.statement: Scolosaurus is an extinct genus of two known species of medium-sized ankylosaurian thyreophoran dinosaurs that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus es un género extinto con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios tireoforos anquilosaurinos que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente entre 76,5 a 75 millones de años, durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus is known from deposits in the lower part of the Dinosaur Park Formation in the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Es conocido de los depósitos de la zona inferior de la Formación Dinosaur Park en el Cretácico Superior de Alberta, Canadá.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaur with a body length of about 6 meters and a weight of about 2 tons.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus es un anquilosaurio de tamaño mediano con una longitud corporal de unos 6 metros y un peso de unas 2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus differs from Anodontosaurus lambei and Euoplocephalus tutus in having a horn on the squamosal that is relatively longer, more posterior, and with a prominent tip.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus se diferencia de Anodontosaurus lambei y Euoplocephalus tutus en la forma del cuerno en el esquamoso, que es relativamente más largo, más posterior y con una punta prominente.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus differs from Euoplocephalus tutus in having small, fused, and rounded dermal ossifications at the bases of the squamosal and quadratojugal.
facts.quote: Se diferencia de Euoplocephalus tutus en que tiene pequeñas osificaciones de la piel fusionadas y redondas en las bases del escamoso y el cuadratoyugal.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus differs from Anodontosaurus lambei, Euoplocephalus tutus, and Dyoplosaurus acutosquameus in possessing a relatively larger iliac preacetabular process.
facts.quote: Se diferencia de Anodontosaurus lambei, Euoplocephalus tutus y Dyoplosaurus acutosquameus posee una hoja frontal relativamente más grande del ilion.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus differs from Anodontosaurus lambei and Euoplocephalus tutus in having relatively large, round osteoderms along the midline of the body with a low central crest and flattened, crescent-shaped osteoderms on the lower part of the neck arches.
facts.quote: Se diferencia de Anodontosaurus lambei y Euoplocephalus tutus en que tiene osteodermos redondos relativamente grandes en la línea media del cuerpo que tienen una cresta baja en el medio y osteodermos aplanados en forma de media luna en la parte inferior de las monturas del cuello.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus differs from Dyoplosaurus acutosquameus in having sacral ribs projecting horizontally laterally and cone-shaped osteoderms with tips located centrally on either side of the tail base.
facts.quote: Se diferencia del Dyoplosaurus acutosquameus en que tiene costillas sacras que se proyectan lateralmente horizontalmente y osteodermos en forma de cono con puntas ubicadas en el centro a los lados de la base de la cola.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus is distinct from Anodontosaurus and Dyoplosaurus by having a tail club that is rounded in cross-section, rather than wider than long or longer than wide.
facts.quote: Es distinto de Anodontosaurus y Dyoplosaurus por un palo de cola redondeado en planta, en lugar de uno más ancho que largo como en el primero, o más largo que ancho como en el segundo pariente.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus differs from Ankylosaurus magniventris in having forward-facing nostrils and lacking a continuous crest between the squamosal horn and the supraorbital.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus difiere de Ankylosaurus magniventris en tener fosas nasales orientadas hacia adelante y la falta de una cresta continua entre el cuerno en el escamoso y el supraorbital.

facts.statement: Penkalski and Blows are thought to have identified two differences between Scolosaurus and Oohkotokia, stating that lateral projections of tail vertebrae are longer in Oohkotokia.
facts.quote: Se cree que Penkalski & Blows identificaron dos diferencias entre Scolosaurus y Oohkotokia. Se dice que las proyecciones laterales de las vértebras de la cola son más largas en Oohkotokia.

facts.statement: Arbour believed a significant comparison between Scolosaurus and Oohkotokia was impossible because only one tail vertebra is known in MOR 433, making it impossible to determine the position of that vertebra and how relative length varies with position.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en MOR 433, solo se conoce una vértebra de la cola donde se puede medir la longitud de estas espinas y se desconoce la posición de esta vértebra en la cola, por lo que Arbor creía que una comparación significativa era imposible, la longitud relativa varía dependiendo de esa posición.

facts.statement: According to Arbour, there is no convincing evidence that Scolosaurus and Oohkotokia differ because the sides of the tail in NHMUK R5161 are not preserved, meaning the features might have been present.
facts.quote: Dado que los lados de la cola de NHMUK R5161 no se han conservado, podría ser que estuvieran presentes allí, por lo que, según Arbor, no hay evidencia convincente de que las dos formas difieran.

facts.statement: In 2018, Penkalski indicated a series of characteristics distinguishing Scolosaurus thronus from Scolosaurus cutleri.
facts.quote: En 2018, Penkalski indicó una serie de características que distinguen a S. thronus de S. cutleri.

facts.statement: In Scolosaurus thronus, the snout plate and the central caputegula between the nasal plates are smaller than in S. cutleri.
facts.quote: La placa del hocico, la caputegula central entre las placas nasales, es más pequeña.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus thronus has eight sacral vertebrae instead of nine.
facts.quote: El sacro tiene ocho vértebras sacras en lugar de nueve.

facts.statement: In Scolosaurus thronus, the dorsal vertebrae are less constricted.
facts.quote: Las vértebras dorsales están menos constreñidas.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus thronus exhibits greater variation in osteoderms compared to S. cutleri.
facts.quote: La variación de los osteodermos es mayor.

facts.statement: In Scolosaurus thronus, the anterior tail osteoderms have a higher keel.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos anteriores de la cola tienen una quilla más alta.

facts.statement: In Scolosaurus thronus, the star-shaped crests or crests of the osteoderms protrude more.
facts.quote: Las crestas en forma de estrella o crestas de los osteodermos sobresalen más.

facts.statement: The holotype of Scolosaurus cutleri preserves six posterior cervical vertebrae, ten "free" vertebrae, four dorsosacral vertebrae, three "true" sacral vertebrae, two sacrococcygeal vertebrae, and thirteen "free" sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Scolosaurus cutleri conserva las seis vértebras cervicales posteriores, diez vértebras "libres", cuatro vértebras dorsosacras, tres vértebras sacras "verdaderas", dos vértebras sacrocaudales y trece vértebras sacras "libres".

facts.statement: The holotype torso of Scolosaurus is nearly completely intact.
facts.quote: El torso del holotipo de Scolosaurus está casi completamente intacto.

facts.statement: It is the only North American ankylosaur specimen where the armor position can be determined with certainty.
facts.quote: Es el único espécimen de anquilosáuridos de América del Norte donde se puede determinar con certeza la posición de la armadura.

facts.statement: The hindquarters show extreme flattening characteristic of Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: La grupa de Scolosaurus muestra maravillosamente el aplanamiento extremo que caracteriza a los Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: The torso is covered on top and sides by armor made of osteoderms, which are skin ossifications not part of the real skeleton.
facts.quote: Este torso está cubierto en la parte superior y los lados por una armadura de osteodermos, osificaciones de la piel que no forman parte del esqueleto real.

facts.statement: The rear armor consists of a large hip shield covering the wide pelvis.
facts.quote: La parte posterior de la armadura consta de un gran escudo de cadera que cubre la amplia pelvis.

facts.statement: Each row of large osteoderms contains seven elements in total.
facts.quote: En total, cada fila tiene siete elementos.

facts.statement: A row of very narrow osteoderms with a low ridge forms a continuous crest along the back midline.
facts.quote: En la línea media hay una fila de osteodermos muy estrechos con una quilla baja estrecha que forma una cresta continua en la espalda.

facts.statement: The neck base features a wide, heavy neck mountain composed of two large plates with large convex but flat osteoderms on each side of the midline and two convex plates with low-ridge osteoderms on the sides.
facts.quote: En la base del cuello hay una montaña de cuello ancho y pesado que se compone de dos placas grandes con osteodermos grandes convexos pero planos a cada lado de la línea media y dos placas convexas con osteodermos de quilla baja en los lados.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus was named by Franz Nopcsa von Felső-Szilvás in 1928 based on holotype NHMUK R.5161.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus fue nombrado por Franz Nopcsa von Felső-Szilvás en 1928, basándose en el holotipo NHMUK R.5161

facts.statement: The skeleton was collected by William E. Cutler in 1914 at the RTMP 80 quarry in Deadlodge Canyon.
facts.quote: El esqueleto fue recolectado por William E. Cutler en 1914 en la Cantera RTMP 80 en Deadlodge Canyon.

facts.statement: The species name cutleri honors its discoverer W. E. Cutler, who was seriously injured when the specimen fell on him while excavating.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, cutleri, honra a su descubridor, W. E. Cutler, quien fue herido de gravedad cuando el espécimen cayó sobre él cuando se encontraba excavándolo.

facts.statement: It was collected from the bottom of the Dinosaur Park Formation, deposited during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 76.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue recolectado del fondo de la Formación Dinosaur Park.en areniscas de grano fino y sedimentos de arcillas de grano fino que se depositaron durante la etapa Campaniense del Cretácico Tardío, hace aproximadamente 76,5 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed in the collection of the Natural History Museum in London, England.
facts.quote: El espécimen de holotipo se encuentra en la colección del Museo de Historia Natural de Londres, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: A 2013 redescription by Paul Penkalski and William T. Blows suggests the genus is a valid taxon.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una redescripción posterior de Scolosaurus publicada en 2013 en la publicación Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences por Paul Penkalski y William T. Blows sugiere que el género es un taxón válido.

facts.statement: In 2018, Penkalski named a second species, Scolosaurus thronus.
facts.quote: En 2018, Penkalski nombró una segunda especie, Scolosaurus thronus.

facts.statement: In 1971, Walter Coombs synonymized the genera Anodontosaurus, Dyoplosaurus, and Scolosaurus with Euoplocephalus tutus.
facts.quote: En 1971, Walter Coombs asumió que había una única especie de anquilosaurio durante la etapa del Campaniense en el Cretácico. Él sinonimizó a los géneros Anodontosaurus, Dyoplosaurus y Scolosaurus con Euoplocephalus tutus.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus cutleri and Euoplocephalus tutus were generally considered the same species, leading to BMNH R.5161 being referred to E. tutus.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus cutleri y Euoplocephalus tutus desde entonces fueron considerados generalmente como una misma especie y por la tanto BMNH R.5161 fue referido a Eu. tutus.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus differs from these specimens in the morphology of its middle cervical ring, osteoderms, and hind limbs.
facts.quote: Scolosaurus difiere de estos especímenes en la morfología de su medio anillo cervical, los osteodermos y los miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: In 1928, Nopcsa assigned the specimen to the family Ankylosauridae and made morphological comparisons with known Dyoplosaurus fossil material.
facts.quote: En 1928, Nopcsa asignó el espécimen a la familia Ankylosauridae y realizó comparaciones morfológicas con el material fósil conocido de Dyoplosaurus.

facts.statement: However, a 2013 redescription by Paul Penkalski and William T. Blows suggested the genus is a valid taxon.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una redescripción de Scolosaurus publicada en 2013 en el Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences por Paul Penkalski y William T. Blows sugirió que el género es un taxón válido.

facts.statement: They concluded Scolosaurus can be distinguished from Euoplocephalus by the shape of its cervical armor, details of other armor, and the structure of the forelimb.
facts.quote: Concluyeron que Scolosaurus se puede distinguir de Euoplocephalus por la forma de su armadura cervical , los detalles de otras armaduras y la estructura de la extremidad anterior.

facts.statement: In 2013, Arbour and Currie reassigned the specimen MOR 433, which formed the basis of the genus Oohkotokia, to Scolosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2013, Arbor y Currie reasignaron el espécimen MOR 433, en el que se basó el género Oohkotokia , a Scolosaurus .

facts.statement: However, this synonymization is controversial because Oohkotokia was later recognized as valid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, esta sinonimización es controvertida ya que posteriormente se reconoció que Oohkotokia era válida.

facts.statement: Scolosaurus belongs to the tribe Euoplocephalini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Euoplocephalini

facts.statement: Scolosaurus is classified within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Scolosaurus is a member of the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Scolosaurus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are four recorded fossil occurrences of Scolosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 4

facts.statement: A 2015 phylogenetic analysis by Victoria Arbor and Phillip J. Currie placed Scolosaurus within a specific clade of Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: El siguiente cladograma se basa en un análisis filogenético de 2015 de Ankylosaurinae realizado por Victoria Arbor y Phillip J. Currie

rejected.statement: The species name cutleri honors W. E. Cutler, who was seriously injured when the holotype fell on him during excavation.
rejected.quote: The specific name, cutleri, honours its discoverer and the collector of the holotype, W. E. Cutler, who was seriously injured when the specimen fell on him as he was excavating it.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'W E Cutler who was seriously injured when'

rejected.statement: Specimen USNM 7943 dates to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 70.6 and 66 million years ago.
rejected.quote: It was collected from terrestrial sediments that are considered to be from the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70.6 to 66 million years old.

rejected.statement: Scolosaurus lived between 83.5 and 70.6 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now northwestern Montana.
rejected.quote: Argon-argon radiometric dating indicates that the Two Medicine Formation was deposited between 83.5 and 70.6 million years ago, during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period, in what is now northwestern Montana.
